                                             August 13, 2026
VIA ONLINE SUBMISSION
Filing Clerk
Public Utility Commission of Texas
1701 North Congress Avenue
Austin, TX 78701

ATTN:
Mr. Thomas Gleeson, Chairman of the Public Utility Commission of Texas
Ms. Kathleen Jackson, Commissioner of the Public Utility Commission of Texas
Ms. Courtney Hjaltman, Commissioner of the Public Utility Commission of Texas
Ms. Morgan Johnson, Commissioner of the Public Utility Commission of Texas
Mr. Patrick Rhode, Commissioner of the Public Utility Commission of Texas

        RE: Review of ERCOT’s Interconnection Processes for Large Loads, Project No. 59142,
        ERCOT’s Requests for Good Cause Exceptions Relating to Batch Zero Deadlines and
        Status Update on Additional Matters Including the Long-Term Load Forecast
Chairman and Commissioners,
First Ammonia LLC (“First Ammonia”) respectfully submits this letter regarding ERCOT’s
Requests for Exceptions Relating to Batch Zero Deadlines as submitted to the Commission in the
above-styled docket on August 10, 2026.1 In its request, ERCOT seeks good cause exceptions
under 16 Tex. Admin. Code (“TAC”) § 25.3(b) from the requirements in ERCOT Planning Guide
§§ 5 and 9 governing Quarterly Stability Assessment and Batch Zero deadlines. With respect to
the latter, ERCOT indicates it requires more time to review and notify developers of dynamic
model deficiencies than allowed by ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.2.2(3)(a) which establishes a
deadline of August 7, 2026 for ERCOT notify an interconnecting large load entity (“ILLE”) of any
deficiencies in its dynamic data submitted for Batch Zero qualification.2 ERCOT indicates that its
request for good cause exception to the August 7 deadline is due to internal processing constraints
and variation in how ILLEs submitted their data.3 ERCOT notes it has been unable to review the


        1
           Project No. 59142, Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc.’s Requests for Good Cause Exceptions
Relating to Batch Zero Deadlines and Status Update on Additional Matters Including the Long-Term Load Forecast
(Aug. 10, 2026) (“ERCOT GCE Letter”).
        2
            Id. at 6.
        3
            Id.

One Rockefeller Plaza | Suite 2416 | New York, New York 10020 |212 464 7114
 dynamic data submissions, which exceed 200 in number, by the applicable deadline, but that
ERCOT will do so and notify ILLEs of any deficiencies therewith as soon as possible.4
ERCOT also indicates that because PGRR 145 was adopted and implemented on a compressed
timeline, not all ILLEs were able to demonstrate strict compliance with all applicable eligibility
criteria, and as a result, ERCOT issued a Market Notice on July 23, 2026 allowing such ILLEs to
explain why it warrants a good cause exception from the applicable criterion.5 ERCOT
acknowledges that the Market Notice expressly states that the requirement to have a qualifying
interconnection study is not subject to the good cause exception process; ERCOT does not state
that the Market Notice omitted any other Batch Zero qualification criteria from this good cause
exception process, nor did the Market Notice indicate that any other criteria were excluded.6
Rather, the Market Notice states only that “[f]or purposes of this Market Notice, eligibility criteria
that may be excepted do not include the requirement in Section 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(i) and (f)(i) that the
Large Load have a complete and valid set of interconnection studies as described in Section 9.2.1.4
or that the Large Load satisfy one of the requirements in Section 9.2.1.2(1)(a)(i)-(iii).”
Despite this, ERCOT’s request for good cause exception to the Commission indicates without
explanation that “ERCOT will also not consider exceptions from the July 10, 2026 deadline for an
ILLE to submit dynamic models for its Large Load.” This means that if an ILLE’s good cause
exception request includes submission of dynamic modeling after July 10, 2026, the Commission
will not even be presented an opportunity to review the ILLE’s request because ERCOT will not
consider it.
First Ammonia respectfully requests that the Commission direct ERCOT not to categorically
exclude from its review of ILLE good cause exception requests those which include reference to
submission of dynamic modeling information after July 10, 2026. Much like ERCOT’s own
request for good cause exception to the Commission regarding internal processing constraints
contributing to ERCOT’s need for more time to review dynamic modeling submissions, individual
ILLEs may have legitimate bases for not meeting the July 10th submission deadline for models –
not the least of which including the 24-hour notice period of the availability of exception from
Batch Zero qualifications which was issued after the July 10th modeling submission deadline
established in PGRR 145. In certain scenarios, good cause may very well exist for the late


        4
            Id. at 6-7.
        5
            Id. at 9.
        6
          Id. See also Market Notice M-B062326-06, Batch Zero Eligibility Submissions and Good Cause Exception
Process for PGRR145 (July 23,2026), https://www.ercot.com/services/comm/mkt_notices/M-13062326-06.

One Rockefeller Plaza | Suite 2416 | New York, New York 10020 |212 464 7114
 submissions. Additionally, the Commission may find it relevant to assess whether failure to comply
with the July 10 deadline to submit dynamic modeling directly to the ERCOT email address for
Batch Zero review creates a substantive issue for Batch Zero qualification purposes. For example,
the dynamic models for First Ammonia’s project seeking Batch Zero qualification were submitted
to ERCOT by its interconnecting transmission service provider as part of its stability study in May
2025 (approved by ERCOT in June 2025), well before the July 10, 2026 deadline in PGRR 145,
and its modeling was the same for Batch Zero purposes when re-submitted to the Batch Zero email
address after July 10, 2026.

As ERCOT is requesting more time to review dynamic models, and as ERCOT has only received
20 eligible requests for good cause exception (all of which may not relate to modeling issues),
First Ammonia suggests that consideration of good cause exceptions related to modeling are not
reasonably prejudicial to implementation of Batch Zero – particularly as ERCOT indicates it may
need “several months” to conduct the data center verification and audit process required by
Governor Abbott’s letter, as referenced in ERCOT’s filing.7

First Ammonia respectfully requests that the Commission leave open the opportunity for its own
review of ILLE good cause exception requests that reference the modeling deadlines of PGRR 145
so it may make an informed decision on a case-by-case basis as appropriate.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

                                                     Sincerely,



                                                     _____________________
                                                     Joel H. Moser
                                                     CEO
                                                     First Ammonia LLC
